title: Fix test AOF duration more tolerance for Mac sleep delay
body:
## Issue

Failed daily CI on 2026-09-17 : https://github.com/redis/redis/actions/runs/35165547793/job/105025700203

AOF duration tests use `2 * delayusec` as max limit. On macOS, nanosleep(50000) sometimes take longer than 50ms. This make correct tests fail even aof_cmd_duration is right.

## Change

Compare AOF duration delta with INFO commandstats real time. The test still check the delay time, and make sure AOF duration is between 50% and 150% of real command time. So it still can catch missing or repeat counting.


## Test

| PR Validation CI Item | PR Validation CI Details |
| --- | --- |
| Executed daily jobs | ubuntu,macos |
| Tests | redis |
| Extra test arguments | --single unit/moduleapi/aofduration |
| CI link | [https://github.com/vitahlin/redis/actions/runs/35191833136](https://github.com/vitahlin/redis/actions/runs/35191833136) |

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Test-only changes to timing assertions in `aofduration.tcl`; no server or module behavior is modified.
> 
> **Overview**
> Relaxes flaky AOF duration module tests on platforms where sleeps run longer than the nominal delay (e.g. macOS).
> 
> Three tests that sleep ~50µs while exercising blocked `RM_Replicate`, nested `RM_Call`, and reply-callback paths no longer cap `aof_cmd_duration` at `2 × delayusec`. They now run through `sum_duration_delta_vs_real`, which pairs the AOF duration delta with the same command’s `INFO commandstats` microseconds, and assert the measured AOF time is still at least the intended delay and within **50%–150%** of that real command time so double-counting checks remain meaningful.
